findings.title: Working-hours check in checkIfIsAvailable uses wrong start/end values, making the check ineffective
findings.body: In the newly added working-hours validation inside `checkIfIsAvailable`, both `start` and `end` are computed identically as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` (lines 141-142). The `end` should be the slot end time (`slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute()`), not a copy of the start. As written, the condition `start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` only rejects slots whose start minute-of-day falls outside the working-hours window; it never rejects a slot that starts inside working hours but extends past the end of the working-hours window (e.g. a 60-minute event starting at the last 30 minutes of an availability block). This means the new working-hours guard — which is the mechanism that makes fixed-host date overrides restrict round-robin slots — fails to block slots that overrun the override/working-hours end, so round-robin events can still be booked at times when the fixed host is unavailable. Fix: compute `end` from `slotEndTime`.

findings.title: Date-override day matching in checkIfIsAvailable uses organizer offset with a sign error and ignores the override's own timeZone
findings.body: The new date-override logic computes `const utcOffset = organizerTimeZone ? dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1 : 0;` and then compares `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` against the slot's UTC day. Two problems: (1) `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()` already returns the offset of that instant in the organizer zone; negating it and adding it to the UTC instant shifts the date in the wrong direction, so the 'which day does this override belong to' comparison is off by the offset (e.g. an override stored as 2023-05-10T00:00:00Z for a UTC+5:30 organizer is treated as belonging to 2023-05-09). (2) The override objects now carry their own `timeZone` (added to the flattened `dateOverrides` at line 410-416 and to the `TimeRange` type), but `checkIfIsAvailable` never reads `date.timeZone`; it only uses the passed `organizerTimeZone`, which for per-user schedules is `schedule.timeZone`/`userSchedule.timeZone` — the user's profile timezone, not necessarily the schedule's timezone the override was created in. Consequences: overrides can be matched to the wrong calendar day (slots wrongly excluded or wrongly allowed), and the day-boundary logic is inconsistent with the timezone-correct conversion added in `packages/lib/slots.ts` (which uses `override.timeZone`). The day-matching should use the override's own `timeZone` (falling back to `organizerTimeZone`) and the correct offset sign, consistent with the slots.ts conversion.

findings.title: Date-override containment checks in checkIfIsAvailable compare instants with `===` on Dayjs objects and mis-handle blocked (zero-length) overrides
findings.body: In the new date-override block, `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` (line 114) compares two distinct Dayjs object instances with `===`, which is always `false` — object identity, not value equality. The intent (per the surrounding logic: a zero-length override means 'blocked/unavailable all day') is to detect a blocked day, but the comparison never fires, so an all-day 'unavailable' override (start === end) falls through to the range checks and the slot is treated as available during the blocked day. The correct check is `.isSame(...)` (or comparing the underlying timestamps). Additionally, the containment logic returns `true` from the `find` callback when the slot is entirely before the override start or entirely after the override end, which makes `dateOverrides.find(...)` truthy and causes `return false` ('slot is not within the date override') — i.e. any slot on a day that has any override but falls outside the override window is rejected, which is correct only if the override replaces the whole day; combined with the broken zero-length check, blocked days and partial overrides interact incorrectly. The comparisons should use `.isSame()`/`.isBefore()`/`.isAfter()` consistently and the zero-length (blocked) case must be handled explicitly.

findings.title: Selected-slot filtering returns false for users with no selected slot when seats are not enabled, inverting the intended logic
findings.body: In the selectedSlots filtering block, the per-user filter does: `if (!busy?.length && eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot === null) { return false; }`. `busy` here is the list of that user's reserved (non-seat) selected slots. For a round-robin/team event without seats (`seatsPerTimeSlot === null`), a user who has no reserved slot is filtered out (`return false`), so `slot.userIds` ends up empty and the slot is dropped by the following `.filter((slot) => !!slot.userIds?.length)` — even though the user is perfectly available. The condition appears inverted: a user with no busy/selected time should be kept (subject to `checkIfIsAvailable`), and it is users with conflicting selected slots who should be removed. As written, whenever any selected slot exists for the event, all slots whose `userIds` include users without a reservation are removed, which can suppress valid availability (or, conversely, fail to suppress users whose reserved slot conflicts, since those users are still passed to `checkIfIsAvailable` with the reduced `busy` list). This directly affects the round-robin fixed-host scenario this PR targets.

findings.title: Date-override activation window uses UTC day boundaries of the invitee day, mismatching overrides stored in organizer-local dates
findings.body: `activeOverrides` is computed as overrides where `dayjs.utc(override.start).isBetween(startOfInviteeDay, startOfInviteeDay.endOf("day"), null, "[)")`. `startOfInviteeDay` is the invitee's local midnight converted to an instant, and `override.start` is a UTC instant derived from an organizer-local date/time. An override created for '2023-05-10 14:00–18:00' in the organizer's timezone is stored as the corresponding UTC instant; whether it falls inside the invitee-day window `[inviteeMidnight, inviteeMidnight+24h)` depends on the invitee's timezone offset relative to the organizer. For invitees whose day window does not contain the override's UTC start instant (e.g. invitee far behind/ahead of the organizer), the override is silently dropped and the normal working hours are used, so the date override has no effect for those timezones — precisely the timezone bug (#8329) this PR claims to fix. The activation check should be based on the override's calendar date in the organizer's timezone (using `override.timeZone`, now available on `TimeRange`) compared against the invitee day converted to the organizer's timezone, not on raw UTC instants against the invitee-day window.

findings.title: Override-to-invitee offset conversion in getSlots uses the override start instant's offsets, which is wrong across DST boundaries and for multi-day offsets
findings.body: The new override conversion computes `organizerUtcOffset = dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` and `inviteeUtcOffset = dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(timeZone).utcOffset()`, then shifts both `override.start` and `override.end` by the same `offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` minutes. The offsets are sampled at the override's start instant only; if the override spans a DST transition in either the organizer's or the invitee's timezone, the end time is shifted by the wrong amount, producing slots at the wrong UTC times (off by the DST delta, typically 60 minutes) for part of the override window. Additionally, `dayjs(override.start.toString())` stringifies a Date in the runtime's local timezone before re-parsing, which can shift the instant depending on the server's TZ — it should operate on the Date/UTC value directly (e.g. `dayjs.utc(override.start).tz(...)`). The conversion should compute the offset per endpoint (start and end separately) using `dayjs(override.start).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` style calls on the actual instants.

findings.title: Fixed-host availability check spreads the whole per-user schedule object, so dateOverrides/workingHours are not scoped to that host
findings.body: The fixed-host filter does `checkIfIsAvailable({ time: slot.time, ...schedule, ...availabilityCheckProps, organizerTimeZone: schedule.timeZone })` where `schedule` is the per-user availability object `{ timeZone, workingHours, dateOverrides, busy, user }`. Because `...schedule` spreads `workingHours` and `dateOverrides` from that user's availability, the new working-hours/date-override checks inside `checkIfIsAvailable` are applied per fixed host — which is the intent — but note that `workingHours` from `getUserAvailability` is the user's raw working hours in minutes-since-midnight in the user's timezone, while `checkIfIsAvailable` compares them against `slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute()` where `slotStartTime = time.utc()` — i.e. UTC minutes-of-day, not organizer-local minutes-of-day. Unless the organizer is in UTC, the working-hours comparison is shifted by the organizer's UTC offset, so the guard rejects/accepts the wrong slots. The minutes-of-day must be computed in the organizer's timezone (`slotStartTime.tz(schedule.timeZone)`), consistent with how the override day-matching attempts to use the organizer timezone.

findings.title: New timezone test only asserts identical UTC output and does not cover a case where the invitee timezone changes the override day
findings.body: The added test `scheduleForEventOnADayWithDateOverrideDifferentTimezone` requests the same UTC window with `timeZone: Timezones["+6:00"]` (Asia/Dhaka, 30 minutes ahead of the organizer's Asia/Kolkata) and asserts the exact same UTC slot list, with the comment 'it should return the same as this is the utc time'. Because the requested `startTime`/`endTime` window is identical and the override (14:00–18:00 'UTC' in the fixture, interpreted via the schedule timezone) does not cross a day boundary between +5:30 and +6:00, this test cannot detect the day-window/offset bugs described in the slots.ts and slots.ts findings — the override start instant still falls within the invitee-day window and the offset math happens to cancel. A meaningful regression test would use an override near midnight in the organizer's timezone (so that a +6:00 or negative-offset invitee sees it on a different calendar day) and assert the slots shift accordingly, and would also cover a blocked (zero-length) override and a fixed-host round-robin scenario, none of which are present in the added tests.
